items.detail: THE organising fact of the whole trip: data that enters China from outside the firewall just works. Airalo, Nomad, Saily or Holafly route through a foreign carrier, so WhatsApp, Gmail, Google Maps and Instagram all work with no VPN. The profile MUST be installed before landing — it cannot be downloaded inside the firewall.

items.item: Hotel and train Wi-Fi is inside the firewall
items.detail: Regardless of your SIM. Connecting to the Westin's Wi-Fi kills WhatsApp until you switch back to cellular. Worth knowing before you blame the eSIM.

items.item: Do not buy a local Chinese SIM on arrival
items.detail: That was right in 2017 and is wrong now. A local SIM sits inside the firewall and would kill WhatsApp — James's only real channel. Passport, 15–30 min, best rural coverage and cheapest data, so it's worth considering for the Tibet leg only, and only if the guide arranges it.

Buy and test before departure — provider sites are blocked inside. 2026 reporting on mainland reliability is mixed after this spring's crackdown on domestic relay servers, so treat it as a spare tyre, not the plan. US carrier roaming day-passes are the other offshore-routed backup for the first hours.

Primary wallet. Visa/Mastercard bind directly. Free up to ¥200 per transaction and ~3% above — so small spend on the wallet, big hotel and ticket charges on the card itself. Carries the metro ride code for both Xi'an and Shanghai, including Line 11 to Disneyland. Institutional cap $5,000/transaction but issuer channel caps ($1,000–2,000) bind first. Passport verification takes 1–3 business days: submit by ~24 Sep.
Not optional — it's the booking channel for several museums and the way people will offer help. Verification is near-instant, unlike Alipay's.
¥300–500 in small bills. Prepaid 'Tour Pass'-style cards carry ~5% load fees — only if direct binding fails.

English mode, for transit and walking. Chinese map data is legally offset from GPS, which is why Google Maps misbehaves even when it loads. Apple Maps works natively in China on a US iPhone — a good fallback.
Download offline packs for Shaanxi, Shanghai and Tibet. The maintained successor to maps.me. On the Tibet leg this is the only mapping to count on.
English interface, pays via Alipay. Mainly for the Hongqiao run on the 10th and the Pudong run on the 15th with the big suitcase.

Z165 is already booked via James. Chinese rail is paperless — board by laying the passport on the gate scanner, no ticket-window collection. Trip.com is the foreign-card fallback if you ever need to buy rail yourself.
Fully offline dictionary — the reliable one at altitude. Baidu Translate as a local-network fallback.

Works only over offshore data — Google withdrew its mainland service. But download the offline Chinese pack: camera translation on menus and signs works offline, which is most of what you need it for.
For restaurants. Skip Meituan — it wants a Chinese number and a domestic bank card.
Optional, free, and saves time in the arrivals hall. National Immigration Administration site, the '移民局12367' app, or the WeChat/Alipay mini-program. Any site charging for it is a scam.
Bonvoy, Delta, Korean Air and China Eastern all work. Screenshot the boarding passes.
